end.summary:
- Practised that a freely suspended magnet settles roughly north–south; the direction was not stated steadily yet.
- Practised making a simple compass and linking its action to Earth behaving like a giant magnet; this still needs checking next time.
- The cold/freezer explanation appeared repeatedly and was not corrected by the end of the lesson.
- Teach-back was not passed; the lesson ended after Mahi said they were tired.
end.parentNote: Mahi practised the north–south direction of a freely suspended magnet and why a simple compass works. They used the Earth-magnetism idea at times, but continued to connect the direction with cold or a freezer, and this was not corrected by the end. At home, try floating a magnetised needle on cork and ask Mahi to observe its direction and explain it using Earth’s magnetism, not temperature.
